# Title Bar AI Summary Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Show `"<tab title> - <AI summary>"` in AITerm's app-drawn title bar for the active terminal tab, where the summary is generated by a one-shot AI call after each `/ai` response settles — mirroring Warp's per-session summary titles, using only frontend changes (no new Rust/backend code).

**Architecture:** A new pure-ish helper (`summarizeConversation`) wraps the existing `invokeAiChat` IPC call with a locale-aware summarization prompt. It's invoked from a new `useEffect` inside `AiPanel`, gated on `!isStreaming && !agentRunning`, and its result flows up through a new `onSummaryUpdate` callback prop threaded `AiPanel` → `TerminalView` → `TerminalApp` — the exact same shape as the existing `agentProgress`/`onAgentProgress` wiring already in this codebase. `TerminalApp` stores it on the in-memory `Tab.aiSummary` field (not persisted) and composes the title bar string from the active tab.

**Tech Stack:** React 19 + TypeScript, Vitest for the new unit tests, no backend changes.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-titlebar-ai-summary-design.md`

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `summarizeTab.ts`**

Create `src/lib/summarizeTab.ts`:

```ts
import { invokeAiChat } from "../ipc/ai";
import { contentToDisplayString } from "../types/attachment";
import type { McpChatMessage } from "../hooks/useMcpChat";
import type { Locale } from "./i18n";

const MAX_CONTEXT_MESSAGES = 10;

function buildSummaryPrompt(messages: McpChatMessage[], locale: Locale): string {
  const recent = messages
    .filter((m) => m.role === "user" || m.role === "assistant")
    .slice(-MAX_CONTEXT_MESSAGES);
  const transcript = recent
    .map((m) => `${m.role}: ${contentToDisplayString(m.content)}`)
    .join("\n");

  return locale === "zh-TW"
    ? `請根據以下對話，用不超過 20 個字生成一句精簡的中文摘要，描述使用者目前在做什麼。不要標點符號結尾、不要加引號、只輸出摘要本身。\n\n${transcript}`
    : `Based on the following conversation, write a concise summary (40 characters or fewer) in English describing what the user is currently doing. No trailing punctuation, no quotes, output only the summary itself.\n\n${transcript}`;
}

/**
 * One-shot AI call that summarizes a terminal tab's recent /ai conversation
 * into a short title-bar-friendly string. Returns null on any failure
 * (network error, provider not configured, empty reply) — callers should
 * treat null as "leave the title bar as it was", never surface an error.
 */
export async function summarizeConversation(
  messages: McpChatMessage[],
  sessionId: string,
  locale: Locale,
): Promise<string | null> {
  const hasAssistantReply = messages.some((m) => m.role === "assistant");
  if (!hasAssistantReply) return null;

  try {
    const prompt = buildSummaryPrompt(messages, locale);
    const reply = await invokeAiChat(
      [{ role: "user", content: prompt }],
      `${sessionId}-summary`,
      undefined,
      false,
      locale,
    );
    const summary = reply.content?.trim();
    return summary || null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}
```

```tsx
  // Regenerate the title-bar summary once an AI turn fully settles (not
  // mid-stream, not mid-agent-loop) and the message count actually grew —
  // the ref guard stops this from re-firing on unrelated re-renders.
  const lastSummarizedCountRef = useRef(0);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (chat.isStreaming || agentRunning) return;
    if (chat.messages.length === 0) return;
    if (chat.messages.length === lastSummarizedCountRef.current) return;
    lastSummarizedCountRef.current = chat.messages.length;
    summarizeConversation(chat.messages, sessionId, locale)
      .then((summary) => {
        if (summary) onSummaryUpdate?.(summary);
      })
      .catch(() => {});
  }, [chat.messages, chat.isStreaming, agentRunning, sessionId, locale, onSummaryUpdate]);
```

## Context

This is Task 3 of a 5-task plan. Tasks 1-2 (already committed) added the `summarizeConversation` helper and the `Tab.aiSummary` field. This task is the one that actually calls the helper, at the right time. `chat` (from `useMcpChat(sessionId)`), `agentRunning` (a local `useState`), and `locale` (from `useLocale()`) are all already in scope in this component — you're not adding any new state for those, just a new `useEffect` and a new `useRef` that consume them. `chat.isStreaming` is a real field on the return value of `useMcpChat` (aliased internally from `isLoading`, but exposed to consumers as `isStreaming` — see `src/hooks/useMcpChat.ts` around its return statement).

**Why the ref guard matters:** `chat.messages` is a new array reference on every render (React state), so without `lastSummarizedCountRef`, this effect could call `summarizeConversation` — and therefore hit the network — every time ANY dependency changes for ANY reason, not just when a new AI turn actually completed. The ref makes re-triggering conditional on the message count having genuinely grown since the last summarization call.

## Context

This is Task 5 of a 5-task plan — the task that makes the feature visible. Tasks 1-4 (already committed) built the summarization helper, the storage field, and the prop-passing chain. `tabs` and `activeId` are already in scope at the point where `<TitleBar />` is currently rendered (they're used immediately below it for `<TabBar tabs={tabs} activeId={activeId} ... />`). `TitleBar`'s `title` prop is optional with a default value of `"AITerm"` (`src/components/TitleBar/index.tsx`) — passing `undefined` explicitly is equivalent to omitting the prop, so this correctly falls back to the app name when there's no active tab (a defensive case that shouldn't normally happen, since there's always an active tab in practice).

Note the local variable is named `activeTabForTitle`, not `activeTab` — this file may already have (or a sibling `useEffect` may already declare) a differently-scoped `const activeTab = tabs.find(...)` elsewhere (e.g. inside a `useEffect` used for PTY tracking); using a distinctly-named variable here avoids any ambiguity about which `activeTab` a reader might be looking at, even though the two would never technically collide since JS scoping would prevent a real conflict.
